checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses.
checklist.evidence: API network error with user info and query in PULSE_API_URL: {"error":"Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?","code":"ConnectionRefused"}, error keys kind,name,code only. Startup log apiUrl without user info. Webhook 500 with a body and a refused connection with credentials and query in the URL: 'webhook responded with status 500', 'webhook request failed' + ConnectionRefused, no URL, query or body text. SMTP stub replies with a marker text to AUTH 535, MAIL 550, RCPT 450/550, DATA 554, EHLO 554, greeting 554 and a non-numeric reply: errors hold codes only, marker present false in 8 of 8. Config and settings errors for bad urlEnv/urlFile, PULSE_API_URL, PULSE_HEALTH_PORT, PULSE_NOTIFY_SMTP_CLIENT_NAME, PULSE_LOG_LEVEL: no value repeated (9 of 9). Ops responses: 'ok', 'polls failing (11 in a row)', /metrics with channel ids and counters only. Findings: security-notify-2026-10-31-2, -5, -9.

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes.
checklist.evidence: notify has no admin or authenticated routes; its only listener is the pulse-kit ops listener, unauthenticated by design. Status order observed with curl -X <method> on the running service: unknown path 404 for GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE, PATCH; /healthz, /readyz, /metrics 405 for any method except GET and HEAD, then 200 or 503.

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write.
checklist.evidence: Ops listener: POST /healthz with 100 MB -> 405 at once, 0 bytes uploaded; GET /metrics with a 500 MB body and GET /healthz with a 500 MB chunked body -> 200, body drained not buffered (RSS 68224 kB before, 71932 kB after); 64 KB header -> 431; no request makes the service write. Outbound: api body over the cap with a false content-length or chunked -> 'GET incidents response is larger than 1000 bytes'; webhook receiver streaming an endless 200 body -> postJson resolves in 2 ms, RSS +2 MB; SMTP server sending an endless reply line -> 'SMTP failed: EPROTOCOL' after 9 ms and 3 MB. Local operator files (config, secret files, state, lock) are read whole without a cap.

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type.
checklist.evidence: parseConfig with 36 hostile values (wrong types, objects that cannot become strings, 10000-deep array, __proto__ keys, out-of-range numbers): 36 of 36 ConfigError. Env readers reject bad values without echo. Contract validateIncident/validateManualIncident with a getter object, a throwing Proxy, Symbol, BigInt, function: all ok:false, none throws. Rendering: Slack mentions, markdown links, CR/LF and Unicode line separators come out escaped in Slack and Teams and as one line in the email subject. Findings: security-notify-2026-10-31-1, -6, -7.

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs.
checklist.evidence: All untrusted data enters as text through JSON.parse (api bodies in contract fetchJson, config, state, lock, takeover marker), which creates data properties only. Contract validators read own data properties only (ownValue, verdict): a getter object gave ok:false with 0 getter runs. notify reads raw.id directly at src/api.ts:160 and :204, only on JSON.parse output.

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers.
checklist.evidence: Allowed targets come only from the operator config: webhook url and statusUrl http(s); Slack/Teams https or loopback http; SMTP login over tls none refused on a remote host. Webhook POST does not follow a 307 ('webhook responded with status 307', 0 requests at the target); Slack and Teams use the same postJson. The api reader follows cross-origin and https-to-http redirects (security-notify-2026-10-31-3). User info in PULSE_API_URL is never sent as basic auth by Bun 1.4.0 (authorization null on first hop and after redirect). Environment lookups: Bun fetch uses HTTP_PROXY for webhook, chat and api calls (note N1). Forwarded headers: not applicable, the ops listener reads only method and path (kit src/ops-server.ts:57); an absolute-form request gets 404.

Ledger writes temp file, fsync, rename (src/ledger.ts:175, :221); 25 kill -9 runs during claim/settle writes left 25 of 25 parseable state files. Lock created with wx; heartbeat via temp and rename. Paths come only from env and config, never from api data. File channel writes one escaped JSON line per notification. Modes under umask 022: state, lock, output 0644, no secrets inside. Finding: fixed temp name opened without O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW (security-notify-2026-10-31-8).

checklist.item: Dependencies, Docker base images and CI actions pinned and approved (`docs/approved-packages.md`).
checklist.evidence: package.json: runtime nodemailer 10.3.1, zod 4.6.7, contract and kit by full SHA; dev biome 2.6.3, lefthook 2.2.2, @types/node 26.6.6, @types/nodemailer 8.0.2, @types/bun 1.4.0, typescript7 npm:typescript@7.0.2, pulse-config by SHA; all exact and approved. bun install --frozen-lockfile --production installs 4 packages with integrity hashes in bun.lock. bun audit: 1 moderate advisory in a dev-only package (note N3). Docker: both stages oven/bun:1.4.0-alpine@sha256:07235578f79ef8c6f97d94aee7938e76f5cdba5f21ae5dbfdd3d3d38058437eb (approved; imagetools inspect shows the tag at the same digest); built image runs as uid=1000(bun) with src, package.json and 4 runtime packages only. CI: reusable check.yml pinned to pulse-config 51e95b0, which pins checkout and setup-bun by SHA with persist-credentials false; the docker job pins actions/checkout@3d3c42e5 (v7.0.1), not the approved pin, without persist-credentials false (security-notify-2026-10-31-10).

findings.title: One malformed api item (an id that String() cannot convert) throws out of the poll and stops every notification
findings.command: Fake api returns one valid new incident and one incident whose id cannot be converted to a string; run one Notifier poll (SEC-1 expectation) and the running service with the ops listener
findings.excerpt: SEC-1 consecutiveFailedPolls=1 validIncidentDelivered=false | service log on every poll: {"level":"error","msg":"poll failed unexpectedly","error":"No default value"} | GET /healthz -> 503 'polls failing (11 in a row)' | the same item in /manual-incidents (src/notifier.ts:331) also blocks automatic incidents

findings.title: Text of a non-JSON api response body reaches the poll error and the 'api poll failed' log line
findings.command: Fake api answers 200 with a body that is not JSON and has a bare word where the parser fails; read /incidents and inspect the error text (SEC-2 expectation). A body that starts with '<' gives only Unrecognized token '<'
findings.excerpt: SEC-2 error: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "<upstream token>"

findings.title: The api reader follows redirects across origins and from https to http
findings.command: An https api with a throwaway certificate answers 302 with a plain-http location on another port; read /incidents (SEC-3 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-3 https api 302 -> plain http host: accepted, requests at the http host: 1

findings.title: The dedupe set of reported malformed items grows without bound, about 1 MB per distinct 1 MB item
findings.command: Fake api returns one distinct large malformed item per poll; 50 polls with a no-op logger, heap measured after forced GC (SEC-4 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-4 50 polls, one distinct 1 MB malformed item each: heap growth 50.6 MB

findings.title: The docker CI job pins actions/checkout to a SHA that is not approved and does not set persist-credentials: false
findings.excerpt: 24: - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1 | persist-credentials count 0 (exit 1) | SHA not in approved list (exit 1); approved: actions/checkout fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 (v5.1.0), always with persist-credentials: false

findings.title: Raw upstream item data (unknown check keys, rejected incident ids) is logged without a size cap
findings.command: Fake api returns a check with a 100000-character unknown key and an incident whose id is a 200 KB object; one poll; measure the logged fields (SEC-5 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-5 check skipped: malformed data: 100061 bytes; incident skipped: malformed data: 200073 bytes

findings.title: failed list throws an uncaught RangeError on an out-of-range time in the state file
findings.command: State file with a failed entry whose at is beyond the Date range; run runCli(["list"]) (SEC-6 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-6 failed list: uncaught RangeError: Invalid Date

findings.title: A reserved channel id is accepted and the ledger writes its keys onto Object.prototype
findings.command: Config with channel id __proto__; parse it and seed the ledger (SEC-7 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-7 config accepts id __proto__: true; Object.prototype gained the key: true

findings.command: Plant a symlink at <state>.tmp that points to another file; seed the ledger (SEC-8 expectation)
findings.excerpt: SEC-8 file behind the planted temp symlink now starts with: {"version":2,"channels":

findings.command: Config with a bare word outside quotes; load it (SEC-9 expectation); state file that is not JSON; run failed list
findings.excerpt: SEC-9 config file <dir>/notify.json is not valid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "<file token>" | pulse-notify: cannot use state file <dir>/state.json: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "<file token>"
